source.title: Gradient Descent with Early Stopping is Provably Robust to Label Noise for Overparameterized Neural Networks
source.authors: Ming-Chen Li; M. Soltanolkotabi; Samet Oymak

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests label corruption and fitting using experiments on deep networks, but its focus and measures are robustness under early stopping, not the original random-label interpolation experiment.
record.gate_note: Figure 4 reports clean-versus-corrupted sample loss distributions and Figure 3 reports training accuracy/loss against distance from initialization; neither measures a listed claim version. The cited random-label fitting result from Zhang et al. is prior work and is not recorded as a row.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own random-label fitting experiments and tests signal-before-noise learning through training trajectories, sample losses, and theoretical guarantees. Its main theoretical method differs from the original empirical studies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. Under the clustered-data assumptions, early-stopped gradient descent recovers true labels near initialization, whereas fitting corruption requires greater displacement and later training. The guarantees concern one-hidden-layer networks; deeper-network experiments corroborate them. For perfectly clustered inputs, corruption is never overfit and early stopping is unnecessary.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments vary label corruption and training duration, including early stopping, but do not reproduce the original random-label experiment as a standalone protocol. The main theoretical analysis uses one-hidden-layer networks and a clustered data model; empirical experiments also use deeper networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Training duration/early stopping changes whether the model remains robust or overfits; higher corruption increases distance from initialization. The paper reports different behavior for 30% and 50% corruption on CIFAR-10 loss distributions.

fits_no_version.finding: More corruption requires greater distance from initialization; the study provides empirical observations and parameter-distance lower bounds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorizing corrupted labels requires larger parameter displacement than learning the underlying clustered signal.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: Several empirical results are presented only in figures without exact values in the text. The experiments do not report exact chance-level test error for the all-random-label condition. The main theoretical guarantees depend on a clustered data model and early stopping.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4c reports Jacobian singular-value distributions before and after training, which do not measure a listed claim version. No other claim-relevant numeric result was stated outside the rows above.

untested.parts: Exact chance-level test error at complete randomization and a fully documented check that every training hyperparameter remains unchanged.
The small constant-factor training-time comparison and convergence time across corruption fractions. Greater distance from initialization does not establish either.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Exact monotonicity and the chance-level endpoint of the long-trained test-error curve cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
Controlled comparisons of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation, including true-label generalization after removing them.
A complete temporal comparison for the CIFAR-10 models; their reported loss histograms are early-stopped snapshots.

missing.what: Theoretical early recovery of true labels under bounded per-cluster corruption, with explicit architecture, cluster-separation, width, and stopping-time assumptions.
Perfectly clustered inputs never overfit conflicting corrupted labels, even with arbitrarily continued training; early stopping is unnecessary in this special case.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. V6 was incorrectly marked untested in the record despite being central to the paper. Missing numerical detail alone does not justify limits_scope. No exact curve values were reconstructed from the text extraction.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report test error at chance in text; numerical train and test values are figure-only. The experiment uses Adadelta rather than an optimizer explicitly identified as stochastic gradient descent.
Does not report a steadily rising test error toward chance while training remains perfectly fit; early-stopped and long-trained models are different conditions.

rows.subject: 4 layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST after randomly corrupting a fraction of training labels; performance shown after 200 epochs of Adadelta.
rows.measure: Training accuracy with respect to corrupted labels; test accuracy also plotted.
rows.value: Near perfect fitting to the corrupted data after 200 epochs; figure-only accuracy values.
rows.note: The paper explicitly says the 4-layer model achieves near-perfect fitting after 200 epochs; exact accuracy at 100% random corruption and test error are not stated in text.
rows.check: Near-perfect fitting after 200 epochs is explicitly reported, including an all-random-label condition. Adadelta does not disqualify this stochastic-gradient experiment. Exact chance-level test performance and all hyperparameter settings cannot be verified from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: 4 layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with varying fractions of randomly corrupted labels and stopped early.

conditions.value: various amounts, including up to 50% discussed in text

rows.measure: Training accuracy on corrupted labels, test accuracy, and training accuracy against ground-truth labels.
rows.value: With early stopping, train accuracy on corrupted labels degrades linearly; test accuracy remains high with significant corruption; ground-truth training accuracy stays around 100% at 50% corruption.
rows.note: Early stopping does not keep training accuracy on corrupted labels perfect; exact plotted values are figure-only.
rows.check: Split the measures: corrupted-label fitting is incomplete under early stopping, qualifying V4; approximately 100% accuracy against true training labels at 50% corruption supports V6's early signal-learning component.

rows.subject: 4 layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with varying fractions of randomly corrupted labels for 200 epochs of Adadelta.
rows.measure: Training accuracy on corrupted labels, test accuracy, and training accuracy against ground-truth labels.
rows.value: Near-perfect fitting to corrupted data; test accuracy and ground-truth training accuracy degrade as corruption increases.
rows.note: The authors describe overfitting after many iterations; plotted values are figure-only. Text does not state that test error rises steadily toward chance.
rows.check: The text reports near-perfect corrupted-label fitting and deteriorating test performance as corruption increases. Missing exact plotted values or a verified chance endpoint is an untested detail, not evidence of a scope limitation.

rows.subject: LENET model
rows.operation_detail: Trained on 3,000 MNIST samples with different amounts of label corruption; training accuracy and loss plotted against relative distance from initialization.
rows.measure: Training accuracy and training loss as a function of distance from initialization.
rows.note: The text says distance from initialization increases with more corruption; this does not measure the V4 test-error trend or perfect fitting.
rows.check: The reported conclusion concerns distance from initialization. Distance is neither training time nor a test-error trend. Without readable curve endpoints, do not infer random-label interpolation from this row.

rows.subject: Resnet-20
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with random label corruption using cross-entropy loss and early stopping.
rows.measure: Distribution of individual sample cross-entropy losses for clean and corrupted samples.
rows.note: The result concerns loss distributions, not training-set fit or test error.
rows.check: Early-stopped clean-versus-corrupted sample losses bear on selective learning of signal before noise, not V4's corruption sweep and test-error trend. This snapshot establishes only the early selective-learning component.

rows.measure: Training error trajectory and loss distributions for clean and corrupted samples.

rows.note: The text does not say training error is zero at this point; figure values are not stated.
